name: Lou Correa
bio: Lou Correa has represented California's 46th district since 2017 and serves on the House Judiciary and Homeland Security committees. He previously served in the California State Assembly, on the Orange County Board of Supervisors and in the California State Senate, and earlier worked in investment banking and real estate. Born in East Los Angeles and raised in Anaheim, he holds economics, law and business degrees.

platform.point: Believes abortion decisions belong to a woman and her doctor, and opposed overturning Roe.
Backs a path to citizenship for Dreamers and introduced a bill to give immigrants and refugees access to legal counsel.
Opposed repealing the Affordable Care Act and deep cuts to Medicaid and Medicare; supports community health clinic funding.
Voted against a 2026 Russia sanctions bill because it would expand presidential tariff authority, which he says raises living costs.
Opposed a FY27 State Department funding bill that cut diplomatic and humanitarian programs, calling diplomacy central to U.S. leadership.
Supports expanded veterans' care and has pushed for medical marijuana access for veterans with PTSD.
Voted to block funding for vehicle kill-switch technology.

economy.evidence: Voted for the Inflation Reduction Act (H.R. 5376) in 2022 and against the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act tax and spending package.

welfare.evidence: Opposed ACA repeal and deep Medicaid and Medicare cuts, and backed permanent continuous Medicaid/CHIP coverage for children and a national Summer EBT program in the FY2023 funding law.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: 100% NARAL rating and opposed overturning Roe v. Wade.

security.evidence: One of four Democrats who voted to block funding for vehicle kill-switch technology.

immigration.evidence: Voted against the House version of the Laken Riley Act (H.R. 29) in January 2025 and supports a path to citizenship for Dreamers.

foreign.evidence: Backed Ukraine security aid in the FY2023 funding law and opposed FY27 cuts to diplomatic programs, citing U.S. leadership against China and Russia.

energy.evidence: Voted for the Inflation Reduction Act's clean-energy package and says he supports EPA clean air and water standards.

tech.evidence: Voted against the 2022 antitrust merger filing fee bill.

education.evidence: General statement: supports expanding college access and resources for all students.

notes: Searched the House issues page, press releases, House roll calls and OC vote coverage; the campaign site lists no issues. No public record found on religion in public life.

name: Steve Cohen
current_role: Broadcast journalist and TV news consultant
bio: Steve Cohen is a San Diego broadcast journalist with about 50 years in television news, including newsroom leadership roles in New York, Detroit, Philadelphia and Los Angeles. He was news director at KUSI-TV for 20 years and has since worked as a TV consultant. He has not held elected office and advanced from the June 2026 primary against incumbent Scott Peters.

platform.point: Wants to expand housing supply and crack down on corporate price manipulation.
Pledges lower drug costs, protection for pre-existing conditions and accountability for insurers.
Commits to defending Social Security and Medicare from cuts.
Opposes earmarks and calls for transparency in federal spending.
Lists a balanced federal budget among his priorities.
Names border security as one of his campaign priorities.

economy.evidence: Pairs a crackdown on corporate price manipulation with opposition to earmarks and wasteful spending.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to defend Social Security and Medicare and protect pre-existing condition coverage.

immigration.evidence: General statement: lists border security among his priorities without specific proposals.

notes: Searched the campaign home, about and news pages plus Times of San Diego and KPBS coverage; no debate, questionnaire or statement on abortion, guns, energy, foreign policy, education or tech was found. Campaign photo URL is inferred from the file name and may be a banner rather than a headshot.

name: Ricardo Cabrera
bio: Ricardo Cabrera is the Republican nominee for California's 51st Congressional District, advancing from the June 2026 primary against incumbent Sara Jacobs. He owns Grace Guard Security, a cybersecurity company, and has not held elected office.

platform.point: Would push for congressional term limits.
Supports stronger ethics standards and transparency so government serves the public rather than insiders.
Pledges to lower grocery, fuel, utility and rent costs for working families.
Would propose legislation easing lending standards so young entrepreneurs can launch businesses.
Wants less regulation and red tape so small businesses can open, grow and hire.
Supports expanding domestic energy production to cut foreign dependence and lower costs.
Calls for more prosecution of violent repeat offenders.
Promises better health care access, faster benefits and job help for veterans.

economy.evidence: General statement: calls for cutting regulations and red tape for small businesses and curbing wasteful spending.

security.evidence: General statement: calls for increased prosecution of violent repeat offenders.

energy.evidence: General statement: supports expanding domestic energy production to lower costs.

notes: Searched every campaign page, KPBS and San Diego news coverage; the site states no positions on immigration, abortion, guns, health care, education, foreign policy or tech. No questionnaire or debate answers were found.

name: Christy Peterson
current_role: Office manager and accountant at a construction company
bio: Christy Peterson is the Republican nominee for Colorado's 1st Congressional District and faces Democrat Melat Kiros in November. A south Denver resident raised on the Front Range, she works in office management and accounting for a construction company. She was the only Republican to seek the nomination and has not held elected office.

platform.point: Runs on safety, economy, education and common sense under the goal of a safe, strong, smart Colorado.
Opposes tax increases and wants to reduce government waste.
Calls for securing the borders.
Wants to end mail-in voting practices.
Supports the U.S. defense relationship with Israel and a peace-through-strength approach.
Wants to make streets safer.
Raises concerns about chemtrails and weather modification.

economy.evidence: Favors free markets and low taxes and opposes tax increases, per her campaign platform as reported.

security.evidence: General statement: wants to make streets safer.

immigration.evidence: General statement: calls for securing the borders.

foreign.evidence: Backs the U.S. defense relationship with Israel and a peace-through-strength stance.

notes: Searched the campaign site, Colorado Politics, Denverite and GoodParty; the site's bio page currently shows unrelated spam, so it was not used. No questionnaire answers or statements on abortion, guns, energy, schools, tech or religion were found.

name: Kelley Dennison
current_role: Licensed massage therapist and small-business owner
bio: Kelley Dennison is a 27-year-old licensed massage therapist and business owner from Estes Park who won the June 2026 Republican primary for Colorado's 2nd Congressional District over Christina Blunt. She is a first-time candidate who previously worked on a congressional campaign, and she faces incumbent Joe Neguse in November.

platform.point: Wants to cut federal spending she links to inflation and end trillion-dollar spending packages.
Backs domestic oil, natural gas and clean energy production to lower energy costs.
Wants more housing supply and fewer federal regulations, with local communities leading.
Supports wildfire mitigation, forest health and watershed protection, with local rather than federal decision-making.
Supports parental rights, school choice including charter, private and home schooling, and expanded trade and apprenticeship programs.
Opposes new restrictions on law-abiding gun owners and wants enforcement focused on violent offenders and trafficking.
Wants existing laws enforced and legal pathways strengthened while treating migrants humanely.
Says parents, not government, should lead decisions on children's education, health care and values.

economy.evidence: Calls for cutting federal spending, regulations and compliance burdens and a lighter tax environment for small businesses.

welfare.evidence: General statement: says families should not need government programs to survive and compassion should not grow dependency.

liberty.evidence: General statement on guns only: opposes sweeping federal firearm restrictions and stresses due process for gun owners; other liberty issues not addressed.

immigration.evidence: Supports enforcing existing law and stronger border security alongside more appealing legal pathways and humane treatment.

energy.evidence: Backs expanded domestic oil and gas alongside clean energy and criticizes anti-energy federal policies and regulation.

education.evidence: Supports parental rights in education and school choice spanning charter, private and home schooling.

faith.evidence: General statement: names faith communities as core community institutions and says leadership should value faith and family.

notes: Read the campaign issue pages and Estes Valley Voice, Post Independent and CPR coverage (CPR blocked). No stated position on abortion, foreign policy or tech regulation was found.

name: Jason Clark
bio: Jason Clark is the Republican nominee for Colorado's 6th Congressional District, chosen by a vacancy committee after primary winner Mel Tewahade withdrew. A lifelong Aurora-area resident, he graduated from West Point in 1992, served in the U.S. Army and later worked as a financial advisor and business owner. He ran for Colorado governor in 2010 as an unaffiliated candidate and in 2014 as a Republican.

platform.point: Describes himself as a free-market libertarian Republican favoring lower taxes and less regulation.
Focuses on rising housing, education and health care costs in Colorado.
Wants to support entrepreneurs, small business owners and developers.
Wants to target criminals and improve conditions along Colfax Avenue.
Supports a diverse energy mix that includes nuclear power.
Favors education reform centered on core subjects and skilled trades.

economy.evidence: Calls himself a free-market libertarian and campaigns on lower taxes and less regulation.

security.evidence: General statement: campaign promises to target criminals and reduce crime on Colfax Avenue.

energy.evidence: Backs a diverse mix including nuclear; in his 2014 governor run he said he did not believe in global warming while promoting hydropower.

notes: Searched the two-page campaign site, Kim Monson Show page and Sentinel Colorado coverage of his earlier governor runs (Westword blocked). No stated position on immigration, abortion, foreign policy, tech, welfare or religion was found.

name: George Austin
bio: George Austin is the Republican nominee for Connecticut's 2nd Congressional District from Suffield, running against incumbent Joe Courtney. He grew up in the construction trade, studied construction management at Central Connecticut State University and has run a contracting business in eastern Connecticut. He is the son of an immigrant from Mexico.

platform.point: Cut wasteful federal spending with a household-budget approach to taxpayer money.
Shore up Social Security and Medicare so they stay solvent for current and future retirees.
Push energy policies that lower utility bills and oppose green-energy policies he says raise costs.
Physical barriers where needed, faster asylum rulings, detention instead of catch-and-release, and a modernized legal visa system.
Bring back shop classes and steer federal funds to apprenticeships and technical training.
Lower taxes and regulations and widen access to homeownership for working families.
Set guardrails on AI so its gains reach American workers rather than only large tech firms.
Protect the unborn and defend Second Amendment rights.

economy.evidence: Campaign calls for lower taxes, fewer regulations and cuts to government waste.

liberty.evidence: Averages opposition to abortion (community norms) with defense of Second Amendment gun rights (individual choice).

security.evidence: General statement: campaign says he backs police and wants to reduce crime.

immigration.evidence: Backs border barriers, detention in place of catch-and-release and faster removals, while supporting modernized legal visas and distinct treatment of long-term residents.

energy.evidence: Wants energy policies focused on lowering utility bills and opposes green-energy policies he says raise costs.

tech.evidence: Calls for AI guardrails so innovation benefits workers and not just tech monopolies.

notes: Read every campaign issue page, the Spanish-language page and a health-care release; WTNH and local newspaper interviews were blocked or paywalled. No stated position on foreign policy, school choice or religion was found, and his Medicare pledge was too general to score welfare.

name: Joseph Arminio
bio: Joseph Arminio is a Wilmington native with a Ph.D. in political science from MIT and a bachelor's degree from Johns Hopkins. He chaired the National Coalition for Defense from 1996 to 2000, did contract work for the Defense Department and American Enterprise Institute, taught at American University and Lincoln University, and published a Maryland newspaper. He has written several books on American policy and history and ran in Maryland's 2008 Republican congressional primary.

platform.point: Proposes an American Prosperity Plan with a one-time private debt jubilee and Treasury-issued greenbacks to cut federal debt.
End open-ended wars, opposes the Iran war, and push Israel toward a two-state solution through a broader Grand Bargain.
Would propose legislation mandating formal debate in grades 9-12 and teaching economic history from primary sources.
Uphold the Second Amendment and read every bill for constitutionality.
Wants in-person Election Day voting with limited exceptions, photo ID and paper ballots.
Agrees with ending sanctuary cities and penalizing officials who block removal of criminal noncitizens.
Pledges to run his office with citizen study groups drawing on all parties and viewpoints.

economy.evidence: Proposes a government-run private debt jubilee and Treasury-issued currency to restructure the economy, while also listing lower taxes as a concern.

liberty.evidence: Guns: pledges to uphold the Second Amendment; abortion: names the unborn among core issues without a specific proposal.

immigration.evidence: Backs ending sanctuary cities and penalties for officials who block removal of criminal noncitizens.

foreign.evidence: Opposes endless wars and the Iran war and wants to reduce foreign entanglements.

notes: Read the campaign home, about and all six issue pages; no news coverage, questionnaire or social accounts were found. His education proposal (a federal debate mandate) does not fit the school-choice scale, and he takes no stated position on energy, tech, welfare or religion.
